SOURCE: "Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever for Question Answering", Gautier Izacard and Edouard Grave (Facebook AI Research / ENS / Inria). ICLR 2021 conference paper, arXiv 2012.04584v2 (4 Aug 2022).

COVERAGE: Read all 44,518 of 44,518 chars across 13 pages: body, Tables 1-8, Appendix A (A.1-A.3, Tables 7-8). References skimmed for origins only. CLAIMS
- claim: The retriever learns from the reader's decoder cross-attention, used as synthetic relevance labels. The reader is Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD) on T5. No query-document labels are needed, only question-answer pairs.
  number: none
  setup: FiD reader, BERT-base bi-encoder retriever with shared question and passage encoder
  quote: "we use the attention activations over the input documents as synthetic labels to train the retriever ... we assume that attention activations are a good proxy for the relevance of documents"
  where: p.1-2
- claim: The best aggregation took the first output token's pre-softmax attention score and averaged it over the passage's input tokens, all decoder layers and all heads. Results were fairly stable across aggregation choices. Max over input tokens did worst, and averaging over all output tokens also did worse.
  number: 64.7 R@5 / 46.8 EM (mean) vs 61.2 / 46.0 (max over tokens) vs 63.5 / 45.8 (mean over output tokens)

LIMITS:
- The method still needs question-answer pairs. It removes only the query-document labels: "does not require additional supervision besides pairs of question and answer".
- The authors doubt their own R@k metric: "It is unclear how well this metric evaluates the retriever performance, since the answer can be contained in a passage without being related to the question."
- Attention-as-relevance is an assumption ("we implicitly make the assumption"). The paper offers one 10-of-100 selection check as evidence, not a validation.
- All ablations use a single iteration on NQ with a BM25 start. There are no seeds and no variance.
- The quality of the starting passages matters a lot ("the quality of the initial document sets plays an important role"). From BERT, the method stays below DPR.
- They did not try re-initialising the retriever between iterations. Table 8 (DPR start) did not re-initialise the reader, so it differs from Table 1.
- The method is tied to an encoder-decoder (FiD) reader's cross-attention. Readers of other kinds are not tested.
- Future work they name: better retriever pre-training (e.g. inverse cloze) and better scoring functions.

BUILDS ON:
- Hinton et al., 2015: knowledge distillation
- Izacard & Grave, 2020: Fusion-in-Decoder
- Karpukhin et al., 2020: DPR, for the bi-encoder design and setup
- Khattab et al., 2020: iterative training, ColBERT-QA
- Dehghani et al., 2017: MSE and max-margin losses with BM25 as teacher
- Lee et al., 2019: open-QA setting, ICT
- Chen et al., 2017: retriever-reader pipeline
- Concurrent work: Yang & Seo, 2020. They distil the DPR reader's passage classifier, a cross-encoder, instead of attention.

CODE: None in the paper. It points to "github.com/facebookresearch/FiD" (p.2). The loss is given only as an equation: KL(G̃ || S̃), with softmax over the passages in D_q and S_θ(q,p)=E(q)ᵀE(p)/√d (p.4-5).

FIGURES: The paper has no figures. The captions script returned nothing. For teaching, Table 1 (iterations, p.6) and Table 6 (aggregation, p.9) are the most useful.

PROBLEMS:
- pypdf printed fontTools warnings, but the text came through intact. Spacing breaks some words ("ret riever"), and math subscripts are flattened (α0,j,k,h).
- The text and the tables disagree in two places.
  - The text claims "+4.5 EM improvement on TriviaQA and +2.3 EM improvement on NaturalQuestions" (p.7) for the DPR start with a large reader. Table 2 gives 72.5 vs FiD-large 67.6 (+4.9) and 54.4 vs 51.4 (+3.0). The paper does not say what the stated gains were measured against.
  - Table 2's BERT-start TriviaQA dev is 62.5, while Table 1's best is 62.3.
- No embedded instructions were found.
